title: Tool / Function Calling
interviewAnswer: Tool calling lets the model choose structured actions while deterministic code performs calculations, database access or external operations. The model orchestrates; the tool remains the source of truth for precise operations.
why: Tool calling is how LLM systems interact reliably with calculators, databases, APIs and deterministic business logic instead of hallucinating actions or numbers.
intuition: The model does not execute arbitrary code by itself. It selects a named tool and produces structured arguments; the application validates and executes the tool, then returns the result to the model.
deepDive: Define narrow tool schemas, validate types/ranges, authenticate separately from the model, enforce permission boundaries and treat tool outputs as untrusted external data. The control loop can be one-shot or agentic. Use deterministic tools for calculations, state changes and source-of-truth retrieval. Add idempotency for side effects and require confirmation for high-impact actions.
workedExample: For a supply-chain copilot, the LLM calls a forecast/reorder function that returns numbers from a deterministic model; it then explains those values rather than inventing them.
commonMistakes: Letting the model directly perform sensitive actions without application-side authorization.
Using free-form text arguments instead of validated schemas.
Calling an LLM for deterministic arithmetic the tool can compute exactly.
followUps: How do you prevent unsafe side effects?
What if the model calls the wrong tool?
How do you evaluate tool-use accuracy?
production: Log tool choice, arguments, result, latency and errors. Add retries/timeouts, permission checks, idempotency keys and human confirmation where consequences matter.

lab.goal: Treat tool calling as structured input validation, not free-form execution.
